newsitem.title: UK: VLCC rates buoyant, others lacklustre.
newsitem.headline: VLCC rates buoyant, others lacklustre.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carrier freight rates were buoyant on Monday but most other sectors were lacklustre, brokers said.
Mideast/Japan rates held steady at a healthy W75, with the Diamond Ace and the Nichiryu, both 240,000 tonnes, fixed at this level for Jomo and MOC respectively, loading on Aug 1 and Aug 16.
VLCCs to Singapore and the Red Sea remained at W70 and to U.K./Cont at about W62.5.
A number of ultra-large vessels (ULCCs) were also heard done, including the 515,000 tonne Kapetan Michalis fixed for BP at W60 on a Mideast/Red Sea voyage, loading Aug 3.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs, meanwhile, were quiet but notionally steady at W65.

Other sectors were quiet in typical Monday trade, with cross-Med 130,000 tonne vessels (Suezmaxes) at W85 and 80,000 tonne ships (Aframaxes) at W120. Inter-U.K./Cont Aframaxes were unchanged at around W100, brokers said.
In the Western hemisphere, 70,000 tonne Caribs/upcoast crude cargoes were steady to slightly weaker at W130, while 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems dipped to W170/175 from W180.
European fuel oil, meanwhile, was mixed, with a lack of cargoes in the Med keeping rates depressed at W180 for 25,000 tonnes, while in the north levels remained relatively firm at W200.
